Luhyny Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyr Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. During the Chmielnicki uprising of 1648-49, 20 of Luhyny's Jews are known to have fled the approaching Cossacks. In January 1918, looters were successfully stopped by armed Jewish self-defense forces — a rare instance in this collection of such defense actually succeeding. By 1926, the town's population was predominantly Jewish, and most city council members were Jewish. Over 700 Jews were murdered by the Nazis in 1941. Although a 1994-95 KSEN survey noted mass graves in this cemetery, no traces of them remain visible today.
